title: Async page teeing + MVCC snapshots to cut dashboard tail latency
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Several tenants have reported intermittent spikes in dashboard query tail latency when scanning long time windows with heavy top-k aggregations. Current mitigations (prefetch, overfetch, shard LRU) reduce median latency but we still see 99th/99.9th percentile spikes during cold index reads or when KV-cache misses align with large page requests.

Goal: Reduce 99th/99.9th percentile latency for paginated dashboard queries by combining a non-blocking cache-warming technique (async page teeing) with read-side MVCC snapshotting so we can serve consistent, fast pages while background warming completes. Target: 99th <= 450ms and 99.9th <= 800ms on p95 throughput test for common tenant workloads (10–50 rps of dashboard queries).

Proposed design:
1) Async page teeing: when a client requests page N that would trigger heavy disk/index work (based on a cheap heuristic: page size + estimated index hops + tenant hotness), the request path forks a background warmer goroutine that fetches necessary index segments and populates the in-memory page cache/KV cache; the foreground handler returns the best-effort result immediately using the current snapshot (see MVCC below) and marks the page as "warming". Subsequent page requests hit warmed cache. Tee requests are rate-limited per-tenant and per-shard to avoid read amplification.

2) MVCC snapshotting: extend the console query API layer to attach a consistent read snapshot ID to multi-page reads. Snapshot creation is cheap (sequence token) and allows foreground responses to be served from a stable logical view even while background warming fetches newer or partial index shards. This avoids locks and avoids clients seeing partially-constructed pages during warming. Snapshots will expire after a short TTL (default 30s) to bound memory.

3) Bloom-indexed precheck: to avoid over-warming, add a small bloom-filter index summary per time-segment that the warmer consults to only fetch shards likely to contribute rows for the current query. This reduces IO for long windows where only a subset of shards matter.

4) Observability & controls: add per-tenant metrics (warming_count, warming_rate, warming_success_ratio, warming_latency, snapshot_count, snapshot_staleness) and a console toggle to disable teeing or lower warming concurrency for specific tenants. Add an alert if warming_rate causes read-amplification > X.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime changes primarily in console query coordinator service and the shard reader: a small async execution pool, per-tenant token bucket, bloom-index lookup during plan stage, and snapshot lifecycle manager.
- Storage layer: leverage existing segment fetch API; warmers will call the same segment fetch but with lower priority IO hints.
- Consistency: clients requesting subsequent pages must include the snapshot token to keep results stable across pages; the SDK will be updated to pass snapshot automatically for multi-page enumerations. Backwards compatibility: if no snapshot token present, behavior remains unchanged.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement feature flag gated warming off by default; enable for internal tenants and a small set of low-risk customers. Instrument detailed metrics. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (gradual rollout): enable for 10% traffic by tenant, monitor 99/99.9th latency and read amplification signals. Tune bloom false-positive rate and warming concurrency. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (full): enable across clusters with tenant-level controls and console UI for toggles and metrics. (1 week)

Acceptance criteria:
- 99th percentile end-to-end dashboard paginated query latency improves to <=450ms in our synthetic tenant workload tests compared to baseline.
- No increase in aggregate read IOPS > 15% attributable to warming under normal traffic.
- Snapshot TTL prevents memory leaks; snapshot_count plateaus and stale snapshots cleared within TTL.

Risks & mitigations:
- Read amplification: mitigate via bloom-index precheck and per-tenant rate limiting. Track warming_success_ratio and throttling events.
- Snapshot TTL misconfiguration: add default safe TTL and an automated eviction sweep.
- Ordering/consistency bugs: add unit tests and integration tests that assert page stability across snapshoted multi-page fetches.

Related artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Async+Page+Teeing+Design, benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console/query-teeing, RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/128
